thread:
customer_acme: Hey team — our org (org_acme_prod) showed 0 credits at 00:00 UTC this morning even though Billing shows next monthly refill at 2025-01-01T00:00-08:00 (PST). We did a paid top-up yesterday and now the API returns 429s for generation requests. Screenshot attached. Anyone seen this?

alice_support: Sorry about that — can you DM the org id? I can take a look at the account state.

customer_acme: Sent org id in DM (org_acme_prod). Repro steps: run a short prompt against /v1/outputs every few secs, started failing right after midnight UTC. UI still shows "next refill: Jan 1, 2025 00:00 PST" though credits column is 0.

quota-bot: (system) Refill event processed for tenant org_acme_prod at 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z, amount: 1,000,000 tokens.

alice_support: Seeing the same on our side: billing event recorded and tokens minted, but API logs show 429 persisted for several requests. Attaching request_id: req_0a1b2c3d and a short logs snippet below.

sam_engineer: paste of error pattern: ```
2025-01-01T00:00:02Z - req_0a1b2c3d - project=org_acme_prod - response=429 - reason="quota_exhausted"
2025-01-01T00:00:08Z - req_0a1b2c3d - project=org_acme_prod - response=429 - cache_miss=true
```

irene_infra: This looks like a cache invalidation race between the billing writer and the API's quota cache. Billing wrote refill at 00:00Z, but edge quota caches (per-region) still had old zero state for ~30s. We saw a small window earlier with high QPS hits from that tenant so token checks continued to return zero.

michael_billing: Confirming: the top-up processed yesterday and the scheduled monthly refill also executed at 00:00Z. On paper the account had credits. Proration/plan-change hooks didn't fire here (no subscription change).

alice_support: Customer-facing summary to share: billing did add tokens at 00:00Z but some API nodes still enforced the old zero quota for a short window due to cache TTL + concurrent burst traffic, which caused visible 429s.

customer_acme: Is there an ETA for when those caches should sync? Our app had a few thousand requests queued and we saw failing calls for ~45s.

irene_infra: Typical propagation is <5s for most nodes but can spike to ~60s if there are many cached shards and high contention. We should have a mitigation: force invalidate tenant caches on refill write. I'll open a small change to the billing->cache invalidation hook.

sam_engineer: Workaround for now (if you hit this again): 1) call the admin credits endpoint to confirm balance: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/org_acme_prod/credits` 2) if it reports non-zero, retry requests after a short jitter/backoff (we saw success after ~60s). 3) or use a short-lived fallback API key tied to a dedicated burst pool if you expect heavy bursts around rollover.

customer_acme: I can repro with a script — will try the credits endpoint next time. Any quick check we can do now?

alice_support: I ran the credits endpoint for you, it returned balance: 1,000,000 tokens at 00:00:03Z. Also cleared the tenant cache from the console which immediately allowed requests to succeed. Please confirm you can run a few calls now.

customer_acme: Confirmed — spike of requests now succeeding. Thanks. Can you also log this as an incident? We rely on refill at midnight, and a 1-minute outage for critical flows is high impact.

alice_support: Logged as INC-2025-0101-01 (low-severity but customer-impacting). Assigned to infra for a fix. Notes: reproduce with high QPS around refill, cache TTL race, mitigation: explicit cache invalidation on billing write + reduce TTL during refill window.

michael_billing: We'll add a billing-side hook to publish a cache-invalidate message to the pubsub topic on any balance-write events (top-ups, monthly refills, proration). This should be in the next patch window (2 weeks).

irene_infra: I'll also add a short-term guard: if we detect a refill event for a tenant, prefer authoritative DB lookup rather than cached quota for the next 90s. Low-risk change.

customer_acme: Appreciate the fast turnaround. One more question: does timezone of the tenant affect when refill is applied? We operate on PST and shift to PST calendar month.

sam_engineer: Our refill semantics: monthly buckets refill at tenant's configured billing anchor (generally the account's timezone/billing cycle). For newly migrated accounts there are edge cases where we normalize to UTC for the write time then publish per-tenant. For this case, the refill was written at 00:00Z which is expected for your tenant configuration. The visible mismatch you saw was purely cache propagation and not a timezone mis-application.

alice_support: Follow-up action items: (1) Billing to emit invalidate message (michael). (2) Infra to implement short-term authoritative-read guard (irene). (3) Support to follow up with customer in 48h after deploy.

customer_acme: Sounds good. Please cc me on the incident. Thanks all :+1:

alice_support: CC'd. Closing thread when follow-up deployed.
